message.reasoning:
I am evaluating a trade offer from p3. I will decide whether to accept, reject, or counter.

I am weighing the trade details. I would give INDIANA_AVENUE and $50 for STATES_AVENUE. This would complete the pink property group. I currently have no monopolies.

Losing Indiana would break the red property set. Virginia remains unowned in the bank, so completing the pink group is still possible.

The trade would cost me roughly $130 in face value. Indiana is worth $220 but I would receive only $140. I cannot complete the red property set without trading with both p1 and p3.

This trade would help p3 complete the red property set. That is more dangerous than completing the pink group, since red properties are more valuable.

p3 would hold two reds and two yellows after the trade. They would not own enough yellows to complete that group. I should keep Indiana to block p3 from completing the red set. I also need to buy Virginia next to finish the pink group.

I am considering a counter-offer. I could offer cash for States instead of giving Indiana. A fair price would be around $150 to $200, since p3 recently bought it for $140. The real problem is that Indiana is my only red property, so giving it away would still block the red set.

p1 has only $28 cash and owns Kentucky, Park Place, Boardwalk, and mortgaged Short Line. p1 rejected a $120 offer for Kentucky. p3 could use that cash to buy Kentucky from p1 and complete the red property set.

I will reject the offer. I cannot give away Indiana to help p3 complete the red set. I previously tried trading Indiana for both yellows, but that deal was too expensive.

I am calculating the cash needed to buy States. A $200 offer would leave me with $474. That barely covers the $450 rent on light blue properties with four houses. I need to verify the exact rent for Park Place with two houses.

I confirmed the exact rent values. Park Place with two houses costs $500, and Boardwalk with three houses costs $1400.

A $200 cash offer would leave me with $474. That barely covers the $450 rent on light blue properties with four houses, but it would not cover the $500 rent on Park Place with two houses.

A $150 cash offer would leave me with $524. That covers both the light blue and Park Place rents safely.

A $10 premium over p3's purchase price of $140 is too low and would likely be rejected.

I will counter the offer rather than reject it outright. I am considering a cash-only bid of $160 to $200 for States, which would leave me with roughly $474 to $514. This keeps Indiana as a red blocker while still acquiring States at a fair price.

A cash-only counter for States would likely be rejected, since p3 wants Indiana to pair with Illinois. I will keep Indiana as a red blocker and offer $200 for States instead. I must remain firm and not reveal my full strategy. I cannot sell St. Charles Place either.

I will not reopen the Indiana trade at a worse price. I am finalizing a $200 cash offer for States while keeping all my properties.

Mortgaging my properties would cover the rent on Park Place with two houses, but that is expensive. A $150 offer would be safer. I am weighing a $175 middle ground against a higher bid to ensure the trade goes through.

I will submit a counter-trade offer of $200 cash for States. I rejected the idea of bidding $220 to match Indiana's value. I am now preparing the tool call.

I am finalizing the counter-trade tool call. The offer is $200 cash for States, with no properties or get-out-of-jail cards involved. I will include a public message stating that Indiana is off the table and that the $200 bid is a clean premium over p3's original purchase price.

I rejected the idea of offering Pennsylvania Railroad for States. I will keep Tennessee as an orange blocker. My next purchases are Virginia, Marvin, New York, and B&O.
